status: proposed - pending human ratification; reviewed 2026-10-22 (see spec/review-2026-10.md), nothing ratified

pdk_inspected.note: The sky130_fd_io survey read the volare install (open_pdks c6d73a35f524070e85faff4a6a9eef49553ebc2b); klt resolved the ciel install above. Issue 4 owns the pin.
pdk_inspected.reinspected: 2026-10-22; same open_pdks f6eeac7d. The deck hash changed because klt gained diode classes and unmodeled-rule disclosure; earlier hash kept above as the record of the original survey.

rows.stretch: Input tolerates a pad voltage up to 5.5 V with VDDIO = 3.3 V
rows.rationale: 3.3 V is the common GPIO level. The foundry user guide states a 1.71-5.5 V VDDIO operating range and a 1.65-5.5 V simulation range, so 3.3 V +/-10% sits inside it. The foundry gpiov2 is NOT over-voltage tolerant (user guide Table 101: 'No'; only gpio_ovtv2 and sio_macro are 'Yes'), so 5 V tolerance has no foundry gpiov2 precedent and is the hardest I/O-rule item: stretch, not target. Provisional until decision 0002 is ratified; see review-2026-10.md gate G3.

rows.target: 1.8 V ±10% (1.62 / 1.80 / 1.98 V), level-shifted inside the pad
rows.rationale: Matches the thin-oxide core devices; the pad cell owns the level shift so the core never sees VDDIO.

rows.target: sky130_fd_pr 5 V gate-oxide devices (nfet_g5v0d10v5 / pfet_g5v0d10v5) operated at <= 3.63 V
rows.stretch: Same flavor; input stage reworked for 5.5 V pad swing
rows.rationale: Thick-oxide devices are the point of this block (CLAUDE.md). The PDK documents model validity for nfet_g5v0d10v5 as VDS 0 to 11.0 V, VGS 0 to 5.5 V, VBS 0 to -5.5 V (pfet mirrored); 3.63 V VDDIO is inside it with margin. Model validity is not an absolute-maximum rating: the PDK publishes no absolute maxima (gate G1).

rows.target: 1.8 V thin-oxide devices (nfet_01v8 / pfet_01v8) for core-side logic and the core half of the level shifter
rows.rationale: Core-side devices never see VDDIO.

rows.target: One ground net VSS shared by I/O and core (common p-substrate); one ground pad type
rows.fallback: Separate VSSIO / VSSD pads joined only through the substrate
rows.rationale: The substrate is shared on this process, so separate ground nets add pad types without isolating anything. Keeps the pad-type pair count at 4 types.

rows.target: Either supply may rise first; with VDD absent and VDDIO present the pad is high-Z and draws <= 1 µA from VDDIO at 25 C
rows.fallback: VDDIO may rise only after VDD
rows.rationale: A pad ring in a real board sees either order. Value is a design target to be confirmed by simulation, not a measured figure.

rows.target: Core-side OE input; pad is high-Z when OE is inactive
rows.rationale: Bidirectional is the README target; the fallback keeps two single-direction cells.

rows.target: Core-side IE input; with IE inactive the core-side input is held at a defined level
rows.rationale: A floating pad must not toggle the core when the receiver is not wanted.

rows.target: One weak pull, selectable pull-up or pull-down, active only while OE is inactive; pull-up and pull-down mutually exclusive
rows.rationale: Pulls give a defined level for unconnected pads. Mutual exclusion avoids a rail-to-rail path through the pad.

rows.target: One fixed strength
rows.rationale: Selectable drive is a documented stretch in the README draft.

rows.target: Fixed edge rate set by GE.3 / GE.4
rows.rationale: As GF.4.

rows.target: Single CMOS-compatible threshold, referenced to VDDIO
rows.rationale: Selectable threshold exists in the foundry cell; kept out of the target to hold the first cell small.

rows.target: Schmitt input, >= 200 mV hysteresis at VDDIO = 3.30 V, tt / 25 C
rows.rationale: Pads see noise from bond wires and the board. Value is a design target.

rows.target: Core 1.8 V to I/O 3.3 V on the output path and I/O 3.3 V to core 1.8 V on the input path, inside the pad cell
rows.rationale: The core interface is 1.8 V only (SUP.2).

rows.target: VOH >= VDDIO - 0.4 V at IOH = -4 mA; corner ss, 125 C, VDDIO 2.97 V, VDD 1.62 V
rows.stretch: IOH = -8 mA in the selectable strong mode
rows.rationale: Slow-process / hot / low-supply is the worst case for drive. 4 mA is a common GPIO class.

rows.target: VOL <= 0.4 V at IOL = 4 mA; same corner as GE.1
rows.stretch: IOL = 8 mA in the strong mode
rows.rationale: As GE.1.

rows.target: tr and tf (20-80 % of VDDIO) <= 3 ns into 10 pF; corner ss, 125 C, VDDIO 2.97 V
rows.rationale: Sets the usable toggle rate (GE.9).

rows.target: tr and tf (20-80 %) >= 0.8 ns into 10 pF; corner ff, -40 C, VDDIO 3.63 V
rows.stretch: Selectable slow mode with a larger minimum
rows.rationale: Limits supply bounce and overshoot at the fast corner. Value is a design target.

rows.target: VIL <= 0.3 x VDDIO and VIH >= 0.7 x VDDIO over all corners
rows.rationale: CMOS-compatible levels at every corner.

rows.target: |I| <= 100 nA at 0 <= VPAD <= VDDIO, 25 C; <= 1 µA at 125 C; corner ff VDDIO 3.63 V
rows.rationale: Leakage is statistical, so it is a Monte Carlo candidate. Pad diodes dominate.

rows.target: <= 5 ns into 10 pF; corner ss, 125 C, VDDIO 2.97 V, VDD 1.62 V
rows.rationale: Includes the level shifter.

rows.target: <= 3 ns; corner ss, 125 C, VDDIO 2.97 V, VDD 1.62 V
rows.rationale: Includes the level shifter.

rows.target: 50 MHz into 10 pF, output and input paths; corner ss, 125 C, low supplies
rows.rationale: Follows from GE.3 (20 ns period for 3 ns edges).

rows.target: 20 kΩ to 60 kΩ at VPAD = VDDIO / 2 (pull-up) or VPAD = VDDIO / 2 (pull-down), all corners
rows.rationale: Weak enough for a driver to override, strong enough to hold a level. Resistance spread is a Monte Carlo candidate.

rows.target: GPIO, VDDIO pad, VDD pad, VSS pad, corner, filler set
rows.fallback: GPIO + one supply pair (VDDIO + VSS) + corner
rows.rationale: From the README draft; the fallback is the close-first set in CLAUDE.md.

rows.target: 80 µm for every pad cell (uniform width)
rows.rationale: A uniform pitch makes ring assembly a placement problem. Foundry GPIO is 80 µm and its power pads 75 µm; cited for comparison in decision 0001, not copied.

rows.parameter: Cell depth (die edge to core side)
rows.rationale: Foundry depth is 197.965 µm (comparison only). Depth is driven by the driver, level shifter and clamp area.

rows.target: Square opening >= 55 µm x 55 µm
rows.fallback: Larger opening as the shuttle requires
rows.rationale: OPEN: the final value comes from the chosen shuttle's pad rule; no shuttle is selected yet. Foundry bare pad outline is 65.4 x 75.4 µm (comparison only).

rows.target: VSS on met5, VDDIO on met4, VDD on met3; each >= 10 µm wide; same layer and y-extent in every cell
rows.rationale: Fixed layer and extent per rail is what makes abutment close the ring (CELL.8). Width is sized against the ESD peak current in decision 0004.
Any ring length that is a multiple of 1 µm can be filled. The foundry library offers the same set; the match is recorded in decision 0001.

rows.target: Square corner cell, edge = cell depth; rails turn 90 degrees with 45-degree chamfered corners; guard rings continuous; no pad
rows.fallback: Corner cell with mitred rails and no clamp
rows.rationale: Chamfers respect the 45-degree angle rule in the deck. A corner carries no pad, so it carries no ESD path.

rows.target: Rails, guard rings and well ties extend to the cell boundary on the same layers and the same y-extent so abutment forms a continuous conductor; no overlap or gap
rows.rationale: The seam is where the tools are weakest (CLAUDE.md); making the rule explicit lets signoff check it.

rows.target: Cell edges and pad centres on the 0.005 µm manufacturing grid; pad pitch is an integer number of µm
rows.rationale: The deck checks 0.005 µm ongrid on every drawn layer.

rows.target: 2 kV HBM, design target only; not a rating
rows.rationale: README target. A silicon property: pre-silicon evidence does not establish it.

rows.target: 100 pF through 1.5 kΩ; 2 kV gives about 1.33 A peak (2000 V / 1500 Ω)
rows.rationale: Standard HBM network. The peak figure ignores the device voltage drop, so it is slightly high.

rows.target: Primary: diode from pad to VDDIO and diode from VSS to pad. Secondary: series resistor into the driver / receiver plus a local clamp at the receiver gate. Supply clamp (ESD.4) closes the loop: pad-positive stress to VSS runs pad, VDDIO diode, VDDIO rail, VDDIO-VSS clamp, VSS (no pad-to-VSS clamp device).
rows.fallback: Diode pair + supply clamp, no secondary stage
rows.rationale: Diode paths are forward conduction, the regime the PDK models cover best, but the diode models are stated valid only for |V| 0 to 5.0 V and carry no current validity range (review-2026-10.md G1). The foundry GPIO documents rail-based ESD with a ~150 ohm series resistor at the core access (comparison only). The series resistance and the local clamp are unsized; see decision 0004.

rows.target: RC-triggered large thick-oxide NMOS clamp, trigger time constant about 1 µs
rows.rationale: The RC clamp turns on in simulation. A grounded-gate clamp relies on snapback, which the models do not represent, so it is fallback and gets less pre-silicon evidence. The ~1 us time constant is an unjustified starting value: the foundry HV clamp documents a 2 us time constant (comparison only). The constant must be justified in simulation against power-up-ramp false triggering and the ESD.2 pulse duration (gate G6); no HBM waveform timing was read from a standard in this review. Clamp device choice (standard nfet_g5v0d10v5, valid to L>=0.5 um in bins, vs esd_nfet_g5v0d10v5, a fixed-geometry model, L 0.55 um) is open.

rows.target: RC-triggered thin-oxide NMOS clamp, trigger time constant about 1 µs
rows.rationale: As ESD.4.

rows.target: No direct clamp; the path runs through VSS via the two supply clamps
rows.fallback: Back-to-back diode pair between VDDIO and VDD
rows.rationale: One fewer element on the discharge path; the cost is a longer path, which the path simulation (ESD.8) covers.

rows.parameter: Stress limit during the HBM pulse
rows.target: During every simulated ESD.2 pulse, no device terminal pair exceeds the PDK model validity range for that device: nfet_g5v0d10v5 VDS <= 11.0 V and VGS <= 5.5 V, pfet_g5v0d10v5 mirrored, esd_nfet_g5v0d10v5 VGS <= 5.0 V, junction diodes |V| <= 5.0 V in reverse. Beyond that range a result is reported 'outside model validity', never as a pass.
rows.rationale: OPEN, partly answered. The PDK documents model validity ranges (sources in review-2026-10.md), not absolute-maximum or oxide-breakdown ratings; no source read states a gate-oxide stress limit or an HBM failure current. The earlier '80% of breakdown' target is withdrawn because no breakdown figure for the 5 V gate oxide was found. Model-parameter breakdown values (bv 11.7 V, ibv 1.06 mA in the diode models) are fit parameters, not ratings. The missing oxide/junction stress limits remain gate G1 and must not be filled with an invented number.

rows.target: Every path in the ESD section of io-ring.md simulated with the PDK models for the ESD.2 pulse; turn-on and current split reported
rows.fallback: Paths P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6 only (pad positive/negative to VSS and VDDIO, VDDIO-VSS, VDD-VSS)
rows.rationale: What pre-silicon evidence can show. Snapback, second breakdown and failure current are not shown.

rows.target: Parallel clamp legs share the stress current within +/-25 % in simulation including rail resistance
rows.rationale: Uneven sharing is the usual early failure in a wide clamp. Value is a design target.

rows.target: No cell, report or document describes any cell as ESD-rated, qualified or compliant; HBM figures are labelled design targets until measured
rows.rationale: CLAUDE.md scope rule.

rows.target: Closed p+ tap ring tied to VSS around every NMOS driver / clamp, closed n+ tap ring tied to VDDIO around every PMOS driver; each ring a single closed annulus
rows.fallback: Ring around the NMOS devices only
rows.rationale: Guard rings are the main latch-up control at an I/O. The closed-annulus check exists in klt (ring-check).

rows.target: Every diffusion within 10 µm (Euclidean) of a qualifying tap, per well island
rows.fallback: 15 µm: the SkyWater rule transcribed in the installed Magic tech file (N-diff to P-tap LU.2, N-diff to P-tap in deep nwell LU.2.1, P-diff to N-tap LU.3); 6 µm applies where the top-level latch-up marker is absent
rows.rationale: Sourced: the installed PDK's Magic tech file (libs.tech/magic/sky130A.tech) checks 15 µm tap-to-diffusion for LU.2 / LU.2.1 / LU.3 and states 6 µm otherwise; the BAG3 tech_params file carries the same figures (3000 and 1200 grid units x 0.005 µm = 15 and 6 µm). The 10 µm target is an INTERIM internal margin below the foundry 15 µm, not a foundry value. Note the foundry rule ids LU.2 / LU.3 collide with this spec's row ids; they are different things. No klt deck checks it (klt-rule-coverage.md).

rows.target: I/O driver wells at least 20 µm from core wells, with the VSS guard ring between
rows.rationale: INTERIM internal value with NO source: no foundry I/O-to-core well spacing rule was found in the PDK, the Magic tech file or the SkyWater documents read. Retained only as a layout-planning margin; it is not a rule and cannot be checked by any deck (gate G4). Replace with a sourced figure or delete before ratification.

rows.target: Every n+ diffusion connected to a pad lies inside a p-type guard ring tied to VSS and within LU.2 of a tap
rows.rationale: Pad diffusion is the injection source for an overshoot or undershoot event.

rows.target: JESD78 class I, +/-100 mA on each I/O at 25 C; a silicon test
rows.rationale: Design target. Not simulated and not verifiable pre-silicon.

rows.target: tt, ff, ss, sf, fs: the model-library sections of the same names in sky130.lib.spice (MOS skew, resistors and capacitors typical)
rows.stretch: Add the RC-skew sections (ll, hh, hl, lh) and the _mm Monte Carlo sections
rows.rationale: Section names confirmed against the installed library; see decision 0003. klt marks ff, ss, sf and fs 'complete: no' because they skew MOS only.
The README target.

rows.target: 75 named corners: 5 process x 3 temperature x 5 supply codes (nn, hh, ll, hl, lh; first letter VDDIO, second VDD). Names are listed in io-ring.json under 'corners'.
rows.fallback: 27 corners: tt, ss, ff x 3 temperatures x {nn, hh, ll}
rows.rationale: Cross-supply codes (hl, lh) are the level-shifter stress points. A named, fixed set makes recorded results comparable.

rows.target: Zero violations from the pinned sky130 deck (klt drc). Rule classes the deck does not check are reported 'not checked', never 'clean'.
rows.stretch: Foundry I/O rules added once klt covers them
rows.rationale: Clean means clean against what the deck checks. See klt-rule-coverage.md.

rows.target: Zero mismatches (klt extract + klt lvs) against the schematic netlist for every device klt can extract. Devices outside the deck's classes (protection diodes) are listed as 'not extracted'.
rows.rationale: Updated 2026-10-22: the current klt sky130 extraction deck recognises eight junction-diode classes (diode_pw2nd_05v5/_lvt/_nvt/_11v0, diode_pd2nw_05v5/_lvt/_hvt/_11v0), closing the earlier gap. Whether the drawn protection diodes extract and match must still be shown on a drawn layout; ESD-flagged devices (areaid.ed) are excluded from diode recognition by design.

rows.target: klt ring-check passes on each guard ring (single closed annulus); klt tap-distance passes at LU.2 per well island
rows.rationale: The tap-distance command exists; the foundry latch-up distance is not in the deck, so the value is LU.2.

rows.target: Each rail net is one connected component through every cell abutment; every well has at least one tie; no floating well
rows.rationale: Updated 2026-10-22: klt documents a rail-continuity and well-tie recipe with the existing klt erc nets/ties spec (cut rail, shorted rails and missing tie are distinct findings). Not yet exercised on a drawn ring; it cannot see everything (see klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md blind spots).

rows.target: Foundry ESD layout rules checked by a named procedure
rows.rationale: The sky130 deck carries no ESD rules; until klt does, this row reads 'not checked'.

rows.target: Every signoff result records the PDK build, the klt version and the deck content hash; results are append-only
rows.rationale: So a result can be reproduced against the same deck.
